messages:
elaine: Heads up — noticed a canary rollout allowed ops/rollback for a subset of users who shouldn't have it. Likely an RBAC change merged last night.
marco: which rollout id? link?
elaine: deploy/feature/async-rollout-42. Deploy-bot started canary at ~12:34 UTC.
deploy-bot: Canary started: deploy/feature/async-rollout-42 (canary=5%) by @marco
marco: omg. did the gate check skip for service accounts?
elaine: logs show auth.checkRole returned true for svc:canary-runner even though role mapping shouldn't grant ops.rollback. snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T12:34:56Z] auth.checkRole(user=svc:canary-runner, role=ops.rollback) -> true
[2026-03-10T12:34:56Z] user_lookup: principal=svc:canary-runner, mapped_roles=[canary-runner, legacy-admin?]
```
priya: legacy-admin? that sounds like the old inheritance rule. did the recent role-refactor change inheritance semantics?
marco: PR #4578 touched role inheritance resolution. It changed merge order to prefer explicit grants but might accidentally pull in legacy groups.
lucas: I just checked the RBAC config in prod kv: looks like canary-runner incorrectly has `inherits: [legacy-admin]` (yaml drift).
claire: where did that drift come from? terraform? manual edit?
marco: likely terraform state out of sync after the refactor. We removed a provider-level default before deploy, the plan didn't catch it.
elaine: two immediate actions: revoke the canary-runner role's ability to call ops.rollback, and pause the canary. can someone do both?
oncall-sre: I'm pausing canary now. pausing -> done.
lucas: revoked ops.rollback in RBAC store and pushed a hotfix (rbac-service 0.34.1) to re-evaluate effective grants.
claire: opening PR to add a gating middleware check so service accounts get an explicit deny unless opt-in. draft: #4622.
priya: we also lost some audit entries for the initial unauthorized rollbacks — looks like KMS-envelope logs have identity redaction when key id rotates. we need to correlate request IDs with KMS logs.
elaine: ugh. that explains missing principal name in audit. can we add request_id -> principal table before KMS envelope?
marco: yes, add short-lived signed binding: request_id maps to principal, encrypted with customer service KMS key, then audit pipeline can surface principal even after envelope rotation.
lucas: will add a migration script to backfill based on available traces. timeline: 2 hours for emergency backfill, PR in review.
claire: tests: add unit for inheritance resolution + e2e that runs a simulated canary with service accounts to assert deny by default.
priya: also recommend rotating any KMS keys used for signing audit bindings — create new key and retire old after backfill.
elaine: assign owners: @lucas emergency revoke/backfill, @claire middleware + PR, @marco terraform state reconcile + postmortem, @priya audit + KMS rotation.
marco: I'll also add a temporary alert: if auth.checkRole returns true for svc:* and role in [ops.*], fire pager.
oncall-sre: alert added. threshold: any match => P1.
elaine: thanks team. once canary fully paused and revoke confirmed, we'll run incident breadcrumbs and file a short postmortem.
lucas: revoke confirmed and canary paused. still gathering exact number of effected requests.
claire: PR #4622 ready for review, includes middleware and unit tests.
priya: started KMS key creation and will coordinate rotation schedule.
elaine: good. keep updates in this thread. add any new logs or screenshots inline. :thumbsup:
